title: Blue highlight disappears after right-click on icons hidden in the System Tray
line: Right-clicking an icon in the System Tray's hidden items keeps it highlighted while its menu is open.
explanation: The hidden items grid draws its highlight on its current index. When an item's context menu opened, keyboard focus left the grid for the menu, and the grid's focus handler reset the current index to -1, so the highlight vanished while the pointer was still on the item. The change only resets the index when focus moves to another item in the popup or the popup itself closes, not when a menu takes focus.

commits.message:
applets/systemtray: keep hidden item highlighted while its menu is open

Opening a context menu for an item in the hidden items view took focus
away from the grid, which reset its current index and so removed the
highlight. Only reset it when focus moves elsewhere or the popup closes.

BUG: 456440

From 089a0ab29a8d0211f71c630de5b8404423a9fe43 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001

Subject: [PATCH] applets/systemtray: keep hidden item highlighted while its
 menu is open

Opening a context menu for an item in the hidden items view took focus
away from the grid, which reset its current index and so removed the
highlight. Only reset it when focus moves elsewhere or the popup closes.

BUG: 456440
---
 applets/systemtray/qml/HiddenItemsView.qml | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/applets/systemtray/qml/HiddenItemsView.qml b/applets/systemtray/qml/HiddenItemsView.qml
index a7e6f967fd..f44df62376 100644
--- a/applets/systemtray/qml/HiddenItemsView.qml
+++ b/applets/systemtray/qml/HiddenItemsView.qml
@@ -67,7 +67,7 @@ PlasmaComponents3.ScrollView {
         onActiveFocusChanged: {
             if (activeFocus && currentIndex === -1) {
                 currentIndex = 0
-            } else if (!activeFocus && currentIndex >= 0) {
+            } else if (!activeFocus && currentIndex >= 0 && (Window.activeFocusItem !== null || !Window.active)) {
                 currentIndex = -1
             }
         }
--

review.text: Keeping currentIndex intact when a context menu takes focus is a clean direction, but checking !Window.active only inside onActiveFocusChanged leaves a stale-highlight bug. Once the context menu opens, hiddenTasks.activeFocus is already false while Window.active stays true (for the transient menu); if the user then clicks a menu action (e.g. Configure) or clicks outside to dismiss the menu and deactivate/close the popup, hiddenTasks.activeFocus does not change again so onActiveFocusChanged never fires. On a pinned popup the blue highlight remains stuck while using other windows, and on an unpinned popup currentIndex stays on the old item instead of resetting to -1 on close.
changes: Also reset hiddenTasks.currentIndex to -1 when the popup window deactivates (Window.active becomes false), e.g. via a Connections block on hiddenTasks.Window.window handling onActiveChanged.

Verify closing the popup directly from an open context menu (clicking outside or triggering a menu entry like Configure) and deactivating a pinned popup while a context menu is open, confirming the highlight clears and reopening starts cleanly.
